name: Leth Cuinn, Leth Moga

attributes.attribute: the northern division of the land
the southern division of the land
cut the island from the east to the west

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Leth Cuinn and Leth Moga are two old divisions of the island of Ireland. A great glacial ridge, the Eiscir Riada, once cut the land from Dublin to Galway. The northern part was called Leth Cuinn and the southern part Leth Moga. The two names mark a division older than the five provinces.

okr.objective: Set out the two halves of the land.
key_results: They are two old divisions of the island of Ireland.
The ridge called the Eiscir Riada cut the land in two.
The north part was named Leth Cuinn.
The south part was named Leth Moga.
